searches.note: Twenty three searches of a share of twenty eight, five left unspent, none the author's. The house's own domain was blocked wherever an independent second source was wanted (laposa.hu, villasandahl.hu and villasandahl.com, villatolnay.hu once each) and allowed only to read the house's own dates and methods (laposa.hu, villatolnay.hu). One search went to bor.hu alone and one to bor.hu and winesofhungary.hu, read as primary through their summaries. No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people and their dates, the classification, the grapes, the sites, the making, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile, no judging superlative, no bare family word, British spelling, no dash).
Where a search contradicted the record it was set right with its source; where a detail was found in no source of this check and rested on the author's reading alone, it was cut or hedged.
Sources whose title or address names a living person were met among the results and are cited neither in the fragment nor here.

tested: The founder's dates: born 1940 in Budapest (Infostart), died 15 May 2021 at 81 (Infostart, Index, Pénzcentrum); kept.
Left Hungary in 1967 (Infostart, by sport aircraft), fortune made abroad (Nigeria, as an engineer: World of Fine Wine and a Hungarian obituary); kept as written.

The Nemesgulács plot: Magyar Bor (bor.hu, primary) says the last surviving stock was the Badacsony co-operative's 0.3 hectare vineyard at Nemesgulács, that cuttings were taken from it and that he bought part of the land, and names him among those who began saving the grape after the change of regime; kept, the plot now named as the co-operative's.

The decline: the town's own page says the variety collection was cleared and only a few thousand vines saved; World of Fine Wine and a Horticulturae paper confirm the near loss and the functionally female flower; reworded, hedged as a local account.
The name: Decanter, Wines of Hungary and the house's importer give the bluish petiole; kept.
The auction: HVG (2016) and Pénzcentrum give his house and two vineyards; the record had much of his estate; changed.
The founding year: one obituary gives a cellar founded in 1992; not two sources, so founded stays empty.

swaps.proposal: Replace Jásdi (Csopak, Balatonfüred-Csopak district) with a house of the Badacsony district itself, Istvándy or Borbély
swaps.why: Jásdi is not of the Badacsony appellation, as the thin region rule asks, though the region page is titled Badacsony (Balaton) and names Csopak. No replacement record has been written or refuted, so the plan keeps Jásdi, whose record now teaches truly that it stands outside the district. The integrator decides. A lead found here: the Borbély family cellar of Badacsonytomaj, first vines in 1981 on a plot given as a wedding gift, refounded in 1996, known for its Kéknyelű Selection (Wine Folly's Hungary guide, hungarianwines.eu); it would double Szeremley's grape unless another wine of the house is chosen. Istvándy would double it too.

swaps.proposal: The wine's name, Olaszrizling to Csobáncz Olaszrizling, house and key kept
swaps.why: The bottle is listed as Balatoni Olaszrizling Csobáncz by WineAlign and merchants; the new name holds the plan's words. The read together agent sets plan.json's wine to match wine.name.

tension: The region's producers line for Szeremley says the house brought Kéknyelű back and set the modern standard for the hill's whites; Magyar Bor names him as one of three who began the saving, and the standard is a judgement. Reported, never edited.
The region summary says Kéknyelű is the district's own treasure and the rare native blue stalk; true in substance, but a judgement. Reported, never edited.
